market_question: Will the Carolina Hurricanes win the 2026 NHL Stanley Cup?
reasoning: No single NHL team has a 37.5% chance to win the Cup a full season out. Even peak dynasties rarely exceed 20% preseason; the Hurricanes are a solid playoff team but not a prohibitive favorite. The market price is a massive overestimation, likely driven by recent playoff performance or thin liquidity, and the true probability is closer to the 7–10% range typical of upper-mid contenders.
evidence_points: Historical preseason Cup odds for top favorites rarely exceed +600 (14.3% implied), and Carolina is not the consensus #1 team.
The league has 32 teams and high parity; a team's true win probability is typically 5–12% even for elite clubs when betting a year ahead.
Low liquidity ($93k) can allow retail bias to push Yes price to an unreasonable level, creating a clear mispricing.
sources_consulted: General knowledge of NHL futures market odds structure (BetMGM, DraftKings historical look)
Understanding of parity in the salary-cap NHL and typical Stanley Cup winner probabilities
